title: Bounded public Bitget futures quote/depth archive feasibility

scope.objective: Find a first-party public historical futures quote/depth file or documented supported read-only listing, then validate at most one small sample.
scope.product_focus: Bitget futures; no claim that any query parameter selection below identifies the intended depth product until confirmed by Bitget.
exclusions: No credentials, cookies, account access, orders, unsupported-method probes, paid procurement, Binance, bulk download, production changes, or executable-price inference from trades/live books.

budget.accounting_note: Fresh-call transaction budget applies to this bounded follow-up; prior requests are identified as already-existing evidence, not this run's new calls. Aggregate byte accounting includes their recorded bodies and duplicate saved responses.

finding.summary: Bitget first-party documentation advertises historical futures order-book depth downloads on its web data-download page, and the page's public client source names a download-listing endpoint. No supported public GET listing or archive file was established, so no sample could be validated.
finding.what_is_supported: The data-download page describes recent-years futures candlestick, transaction, and order-book depth data. The classic futures merge-depth API documentation separately says historical futures depth data can be downloaded on Bitget's web page.
what_is_not_established: Whether a public download file/listing is currently retrievable without using the web UI.
The HTTP method, host/base path, or other transport requirements for the client-referenced listing endpoint.
Whether the failed GET route is a wrong route/configuration, a GET-incompatible endpoint, a transient issue, or an access limitation.
Coverage for BTCUSDT or any other symbol, futures product, date, depth level, BBO fields, or saved research window.
That historical archives do not exist, require login/private access, or that executable-price coverage is complete.
finding.blocker: The official page's client references /statistics/public/download/getPublicDataV2 but does not document its HTTP method or complete supported read-only listing contract in the reviewed excerpts. A GET to that page-relative path returned a Bitget HTML 404 rather than a listing/file. A previously recorded GET to the speculative /v1-prefixed path returned JSON 405, 'The HTTP Method is not supported'; that response does not establish the method for the page-relative path. No non-GET attempt was made.
finding.next_official_step: Ask Bitget through its official support/data-download channel to provide the supported public read-only listing method and exact base URL, a small futures-depth sample and downloadable URL, symbol/product and UTC coverage manifest (including the intended saved window), and the schema/semantics for snapshot versus delta, sequence continuity, bid/ask levels and quantities. If listing requires a non-GET operation, keep it out of this GET-only gate and obtain an explicitly authorized bounded procedure before proceeding.
